sections.name: PowerPointParser (part 1)
sections.title: Slide-by-slide reader
sections.what: Declares the PowerPoint parser and goes through each slide. It collects text from each shape, runs picture text recognition, adds table text, and saves one record per slide that has content.
sections.why: Likely reason: a slide is the natural unit to cite in answers. Reason not stated.
sections.watch_out: Table text is added after all other slide text, so it may not appear where it sits on the slide.

sections.name: PowerPointParser (part 2)
sections.title: Text, picture and table helpers
sections.what: Holds the helpers that read a shape's text, run text recognition on a picture, format a table as lines, and read a slide title. Each one returns blank text rather than failing.
sections.why: Likely reason: one unusual shape should not stop the whole slide. The empty error handling is the only evidence for this.
sections.watch_out: Errors are hidden quietly, so a missing text recognition program produces no visible error.

summary: Reads PowerPoint .pptx slides, pulling out slide text, table text and text inside pictures, with one record per slide.
purpose: Makes slide content searchable, with slide numbers and titles so answers can point to a slide.
why: Likely reason: a slide is a natural citation unit, so each slide becomes its own record. The use of text recognition on pictures suggests slides often hold text as images. Reason not stated in the code.
how: The presentation is opened and each slide is read in turn. Text is collected from each shape on the slide. For picture shapes, text recognition runs to read any words in the image. Table text is collected in a second pass. Each slide that has content becomes one record with its slide number and title. The count is logged and the records are returned. Errors are logged and passed back.
inputs: A path to a .pptx or .ppt file.
outputs: A list of parsed records, one per slide with content. Each carries the slide number and metadata for total slides and slide title.
risks: The .ppt ending is listed, but this library reads only .pptx. Picture text needs the Tesseract program installed on the computer; without it, picture text is skipped with only a debug note. Table text is added after the rest of the slide, so its position is lost. Several helpers hide errors with empty handlers.
debug: If picture text is missing, check that Tesseract is installed and can be found by the program. If an old .ppt file fails, save it as .pptx. Picture errors appear only in the debug log, so turn on debug logging to see them.
